hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: suite and hand attacks
hard_gates.evidence: All G1 tests pass in ./erp verify (verify.log): HTTP isolation (1 h 3 m under load), database, process state, source, non-interference and company isolation. I ran hand attacks as alnoor's administrator against gulfsteel (attack.log section 1). GET, PUT and DELETE on B's company, logo and branch, POST of a branch into B, a workplace switch to B's company or branch, a grant of B's company or branch, GET and PUT on B's administrator's access, a branch filter by B's companyId, a search by B's code and an X-Tenant header all answered 404, 400 or an empty list. B's company version was 773 before and after. db-inspection.txt: erp_app, erp_owner and erp_auth have no SUPERUSER and no BYPASSRLS. Every tenancy table has RLS enabled and forced, with tenant_isolation, plus a RESTRICTIVE company_scope on the company tables. erp_app with no tenant set sees 0 rows everywhere. ./erp tenant create, list and suspend worked (tenant-cli.log). I found no real cross-tenant leak.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: planted tenant leaks in this piece (T1 database policy, T2 logo cache)
hard_gates.evidence: T1 (plants/batchA.diff) adds a permissive SELECT policy on tenancy.user_company_totals. G1DatabaseIsolationTests caught it: 'tenancy.user_company_totals: tenant A sees 3 rows of other tenants', and the standard-policy test failed too (plants/batchA-gates.log). T2 (plants/batchB.diff) adds a static logo cache. G1ProcessStateTests caught it (plants/batchB-gates.log).

hard_gates.gate: G1 company layer: planted cross-company write (C2) and in-tenant company-code oracle (C4)
hard_gates.evidence: C2 (IncludeNewCompanyAsync in branch create) is caught now. G1CompanyIsolationTests reports '113 leaks of company Y: company X administrator -> POST /api/tenancy/branches -> 201' (batchA-gates.log), so the round-2 gap stays fixed. C4 is not caught. It removes the 'needs every company' check from POST /api/tenancy/companies (plants/batchB.diff), and G1CompanyIsolationTests still PASSES with it in place (batchB-gates.log, 15 m 25 s; it ran only 5 write-oracle checks). It is a real oracle. On a host built with the plant over the demo database, an administrator of ALN-DXB alone gets 409 'duplicate' for code ALN-SHJ, which they cannot see, and 201 for a code that exists nowhere. The unplanted demo answers 403 to both (plants/planted-probe.log). Only the module test GrantRulesTests.Only_someone_who_works_in_every_company_creates_a_company... notices (batchB-tenancy-module.log). Likely cause: the write oracle takes only the first 3 'code' values of company Y. Those are branch codes, because tenancy.branches is read before tenancy.companies, so Y's company code is never sent to POST /companies.

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: planted company-access grant faults (P2 own access, P3 stronger target, P4 beyond own branches)
hard_gates.evidence: P2 and P4 are caught by G2CompanyAccessGrantTests (P2-gates.log, P4-gates.log). P3 is not. It removes the 'target holds permissions the caller lacks' refusal (userBeyondOwn), which is exactly round 2's biggest gap, and G2CompanyAccessGrantTests PASSES (plants/P3-gates.log). The gate's only junior works in company X alone, so the separate 'target works in companies you do not' rule refuses first and hides the missing check. It is a real takeover. On the P3 host (plants/host-P3-C4-C3.diff, planted-probe-2.log), a clerk whose role holds only tenancy.access.read and tenancy.access.update, given every company, removed the tenant Administrator from ALN-DXB (200). The Administrator then saw only ALN-AUH,ALN-FZE,ALN-SHJ, and the second administrator could not restore it (400, then 403 userBeyondOwnCompanies). The unplanted demo refuses with 403 userBeyondOwn. Only the module test GrantRulesTests.A_user_holding_only_the_access_permission_cannot_take_access_from_the_administrator catches P3 (P3-tenancy-module.log).

hard_gates.gate: G1/G2 branch scope and screens: planted branch-filter removal (C3) and actions shown without permission (U1, U2)
hard_gates.evidence: C3 (TenancyDbContext.BranchFilterOff => true, plants/batchB.diff) passes every gate I ran: G1CompanyIsolation, G1CompanyScope and all of G2 (batchB-gates.log). On the planted host, an administrator limited to branch AQZ-WH lists AQZ-WH,DEIRA-HQ,DIP-SR and renames DEIRA-HQ (200; the unplanted demo answers 404, planted-probe.log). Only a module test catches it (batchB-tenancy-module.log). U1 (company logo upload and remove offered without tenancy.companies.update, U1.diff) and U2 (branch New and quick-add offered without tenancy.branches.create, U2.diff) pass all 11 tenancy web unit tests (U1-vitest.log, U2-vitest.log). The only e2e check for the read-only user, tenancy.spec.ts lines 84-96, asserts New, Save and a disabled code field. It does not assert logo controls or the branch line. Identity has a screen permission gate with a plant self-test (web/scripts/identity-plant-self-test.mjs); tenancy screens have none. I judged the e2e coverage by reading the spec; I did not rebuild the stack with U1 and U2.

biggest_gap.title: The new company and branch grant rules are guarded only by hand-written module tests: the gates miss three of the planted rule faults, including round 2's takeover
biggest_gap.detail: The product now holds every rule I attacked by hand. A clerk cannot strip the Administrator, a one-company administrator gets the same 403 for a hidden code and an unused code, and a one-branch administrator sees and changes only their branch. The gates that are supposed to cover new endpoints automatically do not check these rules independently. (1) G2CompanyAccessGrantTests passes with the 'target holds permissions the caller lacks' check removed (plant P3). Its only junior works in one company, so the 'target works in companies you do not' rule refuses first. On the planted host, a clerk who works in every company removed the tenant Administrator from ALN-DXB, which is round 2's biggest gap back with every gate green. (2) G1CompanyIsolationTests passes with the 'needs every company' check removed from company create (plant C4). Its write oracle sends only the first three 'code' values of company Y, and those are branch codes, so it never sends Y's company code to POST /companies. The planted host answers 409 for a hidden company's code and 201 for an unused one. (3) No gate attacks branch scope: with the branch filter switched off (plant C3), a one-branch administrator lists and renames the company's other branches. Each fault is caught only by a hand-written test in Erp.Modules.Tenancy.Tests, not by a G1 or G2 gate that would also cover the next module's company- and branch-owned tables. Tenancy screens also have no screen permission gate (plants U1 and U2 pass). For a UAE group running a mainland LLC and a free-zone FZE, these rules are what keep a junior from removing an owner's access to an entity's books. The fix: in the grant gate, test each refusal with an attacker for whom only that rule can apply (for example, a clerk in every company); make the company write oracle send company Y's value for each identifying column of every table, not the first three values found; add a branch-limited attacker to the company attack; and give the tenancy screens the same plant-tested permission gate the identity screens have.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/P3.diff + plants/P3-gates.log (G2CompanyAccessGrantTests Passed) + plants/P3-tenancy-module.log (only GrantRulesTests fails). plants/batchB.diff (T2, C4, C3) + plants/batchB-gates.log (G1CompanyIsolationTests Passed, only process state failed for T2) + plants/batchB-tenancy-module.log. Real-fault proof on a host built with plants/host-P3-C4-C3.diff over the demo database (critic-scripts/probe-planted.mjs): plants/planted-probe-2.log shows 'clerk removes the tenant Administrator from ALN-DXB 200' and 'administrator companies before 5 after ALN-AUH,ALN-FZE,ALN-SHJ'. plants/planted-probe.log shows 'x creates code ALN-SHJ 409' vs 'Z221656 201', and the one-branch administrator listing 'AQZ-WH,DEIRA-HQ,DIP-SR'. The unplanted control answers 403 userBeyondOwn, 403/403 and 404 in the same files. To reproduce: python3 plants/apply.py <clone> P3 && dotnet build && dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~G2CompanyAccessGrantTests passes.

other_findings: Only the creator of a new company gets access to it, so every other whole-workspace administrator loses 'every company' status. On a fresh demo, admin.ar creates 'Before Co' (201); after that the tenant Administrator admin@alnoor gets 403 tenancy.companyNeedsEveryCompany when creating a company (second-admin.log). In my polluted run, the Administrator also became impossible for anyone to manage once they worked in a company others lacked: nobody could restore their access. In Odoo, a new company is not hidden from the other administrators. A UAE group with two finance administrators would get stuck after its first new entity. Consider giving new companies to every user who held every company, or to a configured owner group.

Plant results this round: T1 caught (database), T2 caught (process state), C2 caught (company attack: round 2's gap stays fixed), P1 caught (reviewed map: round 2's gap stays fixed), P2 and P4 caught (grant gate), P5 caught (host refuses to start), P6 caught (catalogue and reviewed map). Missed by every gate: P3, C4 and C3 (each caught only by Erp.Modules.Tenancy.Tests) and U1 and U2 (caught by nothing I ran).

All hand attacks held on the unplanted demo (attack.log): cross-tenant, viewer and no-access users, a one-company administrator (same 403 for a hidden code and an unused code on company create and code change), the access clerk (403 userBeyondOwn), a one-branch administrator (404 for other branches, 403 branchNeedsEveryBranch for both a taken and a free code, grantBeyondOwn), and revocation (the next request answers 404 and the workplace moves).
A one-branch administrator can still PUT the whole company record (200 on ALN-DXB, attack.log section 5). Decide whether company-level edits should need every branch, as code changes already do.
